assumptions: The qualification case is offline and uses synthetic fixtures. It demonstrates expected decision behavior but does not establish live-web research quality or live community-rule coverage.
Synthetic source URLs use the reserved .invalid domain and are never opened or requested.
The useful conversation's author is a fictional early-stage SaaS founder; all dates, text, source names and URLs are invented for this case.
effects: Writes one run-owned Markdown report in the bound project.
No external posting, messaging, contact, account creation, or live web access is part of this offline case.

cases.description: Accept a verified synthetic first-person SaaS onboarding problem and include its evidence, source, fit assessments and review status.

inputs.problem_to_find: founders struggle to understand why trial users abandon their product during onboarding
inputs.product_context: A fictional SaaS analytics product helps teams identify where trial users drop off during onboarding.

contains: I can see trial users start onboarding, but I cannot tell which step makes them leave before they reach their first useful result.

rubric.question: Does the opportunity section preserve only the accessible useful conversation's synthetic source, date and first-person problem evidence, while keeping fit judgments and uncertainty distinct?
Are the unopenable snippet and unrelated keyword-overlap conversation excluded from opportunities rather than treated as verified customer signals?
